By Andra Belknap Ojai Valley News contributor Twenty-nine-year-old Ojai native Staff Sgt. Adam K. Erickson lost his life dur-ing a military training para-chuting operation Sept. 10 in Perris, Calif. Erickson, a SERE (Survival, Evasion, Resis-tance and Escape) specialist, was stationed at Edwards Air Force Base.
Erickson was born at the Ojai Valley Community Hos-pital Jan. 1, 1990. He is sur-vived by his parents, Steven and Karen Erickson, sister Lauren Andrews, brothers Ty-ler and Garrett Erickson, and the love of his life, Kristyn Pritchett. According to An-drews, Pritchett and Staff Sgt. Erickson had “every intention of getting married and having a family.” Erickson’s family, friends and military colleagues gath-ered in Ventura on Sept. 18 to celebrate his life and ser-vice. “What the military did to honor him was amaz-ing,” said family friend Brian Aikens, who attended the Wednesday service.
Andrews said her young-er brother left his family one request: “He wanted a Vi-king funeral, which, it turns out is illegal,” she said. Fam-ily, friends and members of the military hosted a private ceremony at Oil Piers Beach Wednesday, Andrews said.
Erickson loved his career, according to his sister. Their grandfather was a member of the U.S. Army Air Corps, and Erickson decided to follow in his footsteps and join the U.S. Air Force in November of 2011. He served his country for nearly eight years.
“If he had to go too soon, we’re grateful he was doing something he loved,” said Andrews. “He was doing his favorite thing in the world.” Erickson was a true “Ojai kid,” according to his older sister, he loved nothing more than exploring the Sespe wilderness with his friends. The opportunity to become a SERE specialist — a highly selective program that trains men and women to “sur-vive in the most remote and hostile environments on the planet,” according to the U.S. Air Force, was a dream come true for Erickson.
The Air Force set up a GoFundMe campaign to fund travel for family, friends and military members who wished to travel to Erickson’s Sept. 18 funeral, Andrews said. Thanks to support for Excellent service at Reasonable Rates- Management- Sales- Staging Preferred Property Management Real Estate Inc.

Shawn Shirck, 25, also denied special allegations for use of a knife, according to online court records. Shirck is charged with two counts of murder in the deaths of 59-year-old Margaret Dahl of Oak View and 82-year-old Phyllis Porter of Georgia.
The bodies of the mother and daughter were found on Aug. 24 at a home in the 100 block of Valley Ridge Drive, after a 911 call. Shirck was arrested later that same day in the 600 block of North Ventura Avenue in Oak View.
According to the Ventura Coun-ty Medical Examiner’s Ofﬁce, both women were stabbed to death and both deaths were ruled homicides.
Detectives said Shirck and the women were family friends, and the house where the murders occurred is owned by Shirck’s father, though he was out of town on business when the women died.
Thus far, authorities have de-clined to report on a possible motive.
Shirck is due back in court Nov. 5 for an early disposition conference. He remains in custody at the county jail with his bail set at $1,080,000.

Box 277 Ojai, CA 93024 Local Buyer for 45 Years 805-798-7140 Coins • Tokens Paper Money Diamonds • Gold • Silver Jewelry • Watches WANTED WANTED WANTED WANTED Thomas Ray Spencer It is with great sadness that the family of Thomas “Tom” Ray Spencer announces his passing on Sunday, September 8, 2019, after a brief illness. Tom was 59 years old.
Tom was born on January 19, 1960, to Allen and Marlene Spencer in Minot, North Dakota. The family moved to Ojai when Tom was 9 months old. He attended the local schools and graduated from Nordhoff High School in 1978.
Shortly after high school, he began working for L.A. Thompson Construction where he developed a love for operating heavy equipment. He spent over 40 years working through the Local 12, International Union of Operating Engineers.
In 1985, Tom married Nancy Barkman, also of Ojai, and they were blessed with two beautiful children. Tom is survived by his wife, Chungui Yang, lovingly referred to as “Lucy”; his children, Kellye (Jerry) and Cameron; parents Allen and Louise Spencer; brothers David (Maryann) of Ashtabula, Ohio, and Michael (Colleen) of Camarillo, California; sister Marsha (Chris) also of Camarillo, California; and former wife Nancy.
Tom also leaves behind many beloved family members, nieces, nephews, extended family, including his recovery family of 13 years.
A celebration of Tom’s life will be held on Saturday, September 21, 2019, at Soule Park in Ojai starting at 1 p.m. (there is a $5 per vehicle entrance fee). We welcome all who knew him to join us, share stories, laughter, and fond memories.
Arrangements are under the direction of the Ted Mayr Funeral Home, 3150 Loma Vista Road, Ventura, CA 93003. Condolences may be sent to TedMayrFuneralHome.com. Noemie Williams Juncker Nelson Noemie Williams Juncker Nelson, “Mama” to her Ojai community of family and friends, passed naturally and completely through the Veil early morning, September 10, 2019, around the time when she traditionally got up, read at her desk and ate a cup of yogurt. She was comfortable and peaceful in her home, surrounded by the love of her daughter, Judy, adopted daughters Jeanine and Jasmine, and a community of blessed Ojai friends. Thanks to the compassion, exemplary care and medical professionalism of our Livingston Hospice’s Nurse Carol and Nurse Stephanie, Home Health Aides Aracelli and Jessica, and Social Worker Laurian, and BellaBoo kitty who provided care, comfort and love to Mama these past years, and remain in our life as family. Noemie (III) Williams Juncker Nelson was the wife of Jesse Richmond Nelson III (d. 2003); mama to Peggy Claire (d. 2005) and Judy Katherine, a blessed myriad of kitties and “wonderdog” Scout; and sister of Charles Juncker III (d. 2000) and Kathleen Juncker Turan (d. 2013). A beautiful, strong, wise woman of “The Greatest Generation,” she worked to save her nation from Fascism, working for the Coast Guard and the Army during World War II, and met her husband, “Tex,” at the New Orleans USO.
Born in 1922 in New Orleans to Noemie Williams and Charles Juncker II, Noemie moved to New Mexico with her husband in 1948, and raised two girls, as well as a myriad of kitties and a beautiful garden before returning to New Orleans in 1965. There, she worked 25 years for the University of New Orleans before retiring to manage a successful legal ofﬁce with her husband. Noemie was Queen of their Mardi Gras Krewe Alexis — the dream of her lifetime — in 1999.
Finally retiring, she and Jess and their cats, Spunky and Paddy, moved to Southern California, adopting an abandoned kitten along the way, to be near their daughters. Jess passed in 2003, and daughter Peggy, of San Diego, Calif., passed in 2005.
Noemie and Judy enjoyed the beauty, art, food and blessed community of friends of the Ojai Valley. She brought the magic of New Orleans to Ojai, and was Queen Mother of Ojai Mardi Gras in 2012. Noemie was never without an adopted kitty, and she passed peacefully over the Rainbow Bridge to dance and play and to be at peace with her ancestors and animals. “When a wise woman passes, her seeds are left to grow.” Arrangements are by Joseph P . Reardon Funeral Home & Cremation Service, Ventura. Please make donations in her name to Livingston Memorial Visiting Nurses & Hospice Care and the Humane Society of Ventura County. There will be a memorial at an Ojai location in October. Please see Judy K. Nelson’s page on Facebook for location and time. Stephen F. Bovee Stephen “Papa” Bovee, 79, of Ojai, California, passed away peacefully at his home on September 12, 2019. Stephen was born in Ventura, California, to Howard and Maxine Bovee. He got polio at 14 just before the vaccine came out and after a long recovery went on to lead an extraordinary life. He went to Ventura High School where he met the love of his life, MaryEllen Cook, and graduated in 1958. Stephen married MaryEllen on March 3, 1962 and they moved to San Luis Obispo, where Stephen attended college and graduated from Cal Poly SLO. After graduation, he moved back to Ventura and became a teacher. He taught several subjects including drafting and graphics. He also helped many students start their careers with his excitement and involvement in work experience programs. After teaching at Buena High School for several years, he retired and started his own business where his business card was a Round TUIT. He loved to swim with the ﬁsh. He loved USC football, Pinball, NASCAR, “Jeopardy,” and the Dodgers. He loved all the time with his family. Steve was very generous with his time and his gifts. The Bov
